_what: Everything the files core knows about the files contract and the folder it shows, as DATA (src/data.rs reads it once). The core names no operation, field, status, word or number in code: each is here. `call` is how one call travels: through the engine's one door (POST to the door's origin, the one thing the shell's setup names, plus `path`), as the JSON-RPC message `body` with each `slots` value filled: the request's number, its request key (BLAKE3 of the door's origin, the request's number and the time it was sent, so a send is never mistaken for an earlier one), and the target's method and input (a call names its method, never an address: the door finds the method's owner, door plan D1.3). `files` is the target of every contract operation: live-namespace's session, reached as a session call (trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools/sessions.rs), its input naming the operation and its arguments (a name never travels in a URL: f1 bug 20), its own reply inside the door's (`files.answer`). `this_computer` is the call that names this computer, and the fields of its answer holding its id (as pin rule rows name a device) and its name (in a conflict copy's name): the files session's own `this_computer` op, which the engine fills from this computer (trillion-rust a7915429a9). When it answers no id (a run the engine did not start), no computer is named, and then a pin and a conflict copy, which both name a computer, are refused as `not_offered` and a listing asks no `kept`. `answer` (and a target's own `answer`) points into an answer: `result` the operation's answer, `refused` whether it is a refusal, whose `result` is then {code, outcome}, and `protocol_refusal` the code of a JSON-RPC error. `operations` maps each job of the core to the contract operation that does it; one the contract does not offer yet is null, and the core refuses that job as `not_offered` instead of doing it another way. `fields` are the names of the fields the core reads from a contract answer and writes into a request. `refusals` map a refusal's code (and its outcome, when the row names one) to the one OS-neutral problem set every shell maps to its own (src/errors.rs); `protocol_refusals` do the same for a JSON-RPC error's code. A refusal the rows do not name, and an answer that is not the door's, are `unreachable` (namespace_unavailable, namespace_origin_not_bound from a copy that may not write the real store, an outcome the door could not learn). No HTTP status is read: the door answers every refusal in its body. `root` is the one place a core shows, the whole of the person's files: the id `ready` gives the shell for it, the name shown and its contract folder. `identity` is the content identity form (BLAKE3, the contract's `1f:` multihash prefix, tools/live-namespace/src/account_files/write.rs). `upload_id_hex_chars` is the contract's upload id length (write.rs validate_upload_id). The numbers the core plans with are the contract's own `bounds` call (operations.bounds), asked once before the first job. `absent_version` is the `expected_version` that says a name must not exist yet (account-files-routes.json `_folder`). Pins are the contract's own pin rule rows naming items (`pin_*` fields; the contract answers `kept` per name for the device that asks); `trash_id` is the OS's trash container, which lists nothing (deleted names go to the contract's set-aside tree, Recently Deleted). `item_kinds` are the contract's row kinds. `conflict_name` writes the plain name a conflicting edit is kept under, beside the other version: {stem}, {device}, {date} and {ext}; `conflict_name_again` the same when that name is taken too, with {n} counting from `conflict_first_again`. `problem_words` is the one plain sentence a person reads for each problem; the `failed` command carries it as `words`, and `ready` carries the whole table as `problem_words` for a problem the shell itself finds (`answer_incomplete`), so every shell shows the same words and holds none of its own. `tail` is the end of a file read together with its first bytes, for every file larger than that first read, as old Trillion did with no gate: a video keeps its index at its end (an MP4 moov box, a camera original's frame table, whatever its media type says), and so do a zip's directory and a PDF's cross-reference table, and a reader asks for it next, so it is already on its way. `bytes` is old Trillion's own number for it (src/namespace-chunk-cache.json `tail_bytes`, 4 MiB, the read path that played a 33 GB file with 17 MB fetched, commit 40696f077e). A span is read raw (`fields.span_raw` true, and the door's `call.accept` names octet-stream): its answer's body is exactly the span's bytes, of `raw.content_type`, with the file's size, the span's offset and the content identity it was read from in the headers `raw.total`, `raw.offset` and `raw.identity` (engine 7e0fbe2ec5); a refusal is still the JSON tool result. A raw read is streamed, so its only bound is the store's own `span_most` (engine fe32a25710, cce39615b0). An upload's piece crosses raw the other way (`call.raw_upload`): its bytes are the request's body, of `content_type`, and the door's message rides beside them in the header `header`, base64url; the door spools the body and hands it to the files session as the piece's content (the engine's src/mcp/upload.rs, at most its `upload_most_bytes` a body), since a session reads one bounded message a line and a piece inside it as base64 could be only a few tens of KiB.

problem_words.unauthorised: Sign in to Trillion again to reach your files.
problem_words.forbidden: You can look at this, but not change it.
problem_words.missing: This isn't in your files anymore.
problem_words.stale_version: This changed somewhere else. Open it again to see the newest version.
problem_words.unreachable: Your files can't be reached right now.
problem_words.invalid: Trillion couldn't do this with this item.
problem_words.refused_copy: This came back wrong, so nothing was changed. Try again.
problem_words.not_offered: Your files can't do this yet.
problem_words.answer_incomplete: Something went wrong reading your files. Try again.
